children: Swiss pharmaceutical giant Novartis AG (NVS, Financials) has reportedly suspended eight clinical trials of an experimental CAR-T treatment, after three patients died.

In late August, Novartis stopped the trials after learning of the deaths, The Wall Street Journal said. The trials were investigating the treatment in autoimmune disease and neurological disease. The size of the pause matters to investors.
This is a failure of one study. It's stated that eight trials have been suspended. This raises wider questions regarding the safety profile and development schedule of the experimental platform.

CAR-T treatments have already revolutionized sections of cancer treatment, and drugmakers are now investigating whether similar approaches can work for autoimmune illnesses. That might be a huge potential, but safety remains a big challenge.

The recent revelation might halt Novartis' work in the field while investigators look into whether the deaths were linked to the medication and what, if any, changes need to be made before trials can resume.

The pause also matters for competitors taking similar tactics, including Bristol Myers Squibb. Investors will now want more details from Novartis about what led to the deaths, negotiations with regulators and if the eight studies can continue.

title: Novartis Halts Eight Trials After Three Patient Deaths
